observations.statement: HITL-035 makes HITL a consumer of the shared permission ladder and blocked-episode model; /ask-flow and /question/terminal are labels over that model, not local state machines.
HITL-035 is classified GUI-related because approval affordances, permission or question prompts, terminal blocked-state handling, and approval labels are user-visible.
HITL-001 is an accepted compatibility disposition retired to migration-lineage-only coverage; it must not re-own atomized product coverage or use the former source-preserving compile mode.

The migration section names an original hash and four run-scoped proof artifacts, asserts no residual source-preserving product coverage, and records that the batches did not refresh governance artifacts or create build tasks.
HITL-036 defines HITL checkpoints as opt-in additions that are not required for default hands-off correctness and must not replace internal audit, test, source-control, or repair loops.
Configured checkpoints may pause for credentials, secrets, or other critical authority blockers only when HITL policy enables the pause or critical-escalation policy requires it.

HITL-037 directs the controller to resolve evidence-supported gaps, apply recorded safe defaults, defer downstream details, classify gaps into eight named classes, and reserve user blocking for a narrow set of policy, risk, authority, credential, legal, or preference conflicts.

HITL-037 requires a durable, explicitly approved testing_policy_override for testing restrictions and permits incomplete work only through a user_approved_incomplete_item carrying named accountability and reopen data.
A valid PAUSE.md gate blocks new in-scope mutations until removal or expiry; an exact allowed action is the only stated exception, and PAUSE is evaluated before HITL.

The addendum enumerates HITLRequest fields and six request_kind values, and it requires provider correlation to use provider-supplied values while representing absence with nulls rather than invented local identifiers.
Skip-node and abort-run UI payloads use namespaced command identifiers and named payload fields, and the unqualified command names are prohibited.
The addendum defines one-hour and twenty-four-hour default timeout values and maps timeout to hitl_request_expired with three named follow-up actions selected according to request kind.

The FABLE addendum explicitly disclaims WorkNodes, runtime artifacts, implementation output, PNC-019 receipts, and a passing buildability gate; its audit-lineage note says repair requires concrete contract evidence or an explicit non-repair disposition.

candidate_findings.title: HITL-035 leaves shared contract dependencies out of dependency metadata
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-035 declares depends_on empty while its normative text consumes shared question, permission, and terminal state machines and preserves ContractRefs to Permissions_System and Tools.
candidate_findings.impact: Dependency indexing or build sequencing can treat the unit as self-contained and fail to require the shared contracts whose behavior it must preserve.

candidate_findings.title: HITL-035 has no exact GUI interaction or accessibility contract
candidate_findings.statement: The unit marks approval prompts and blocked-state handling as user-visible, but its acceptance criteria cover source traceability and non-generation only; they do not define visible states, available actions, prompt copy, focus behavior, accessibility semantics, or a GUI acceptance oracle.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders retain consequential discretion over how approvals, questions, and terminal blocks appear and behave, so consumer alignment can diverge even while the listed plan validators pass.

candidate_findings.title: Configured HITL checkpoint behavior is not operationally specified
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-036 names checkpoint categories and policy-gated pauses but does not define the checkpoint configuration shape, selection rules, event-to-checkpoint mapping, ordering, pending state, approval actions, continuation transition, cancellation, retry, expiry, or concurrent-checkpoint behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent implementations can pause at different seams or resume differently while all claiming compliance, and a bad interpretation can either interrupt hands-off correctness or bypass intended authority stops.

candidate_findings.title: HITL-036 dependency metadata omits one consumed policy owner
candidate_findings.statement: The canonical behavior consumes both Permissions_System critical-escalation policy and Goal_Runtime_System autonomy policy, and both appear in implementation surfaces, but depends_on lists only PS-116.
candidate_findings.impact: Plan graph ordering and readiness checks cannot enforce the Goal Runtime dependency expressed by the behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Checkpoint acceptance is not tied to an executable behavior oracle
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-036 acceptance criteria restate mode boundaries, while its only concrete validation command is the general plans gate and the other validation surface is merely future HITL checkpoint review.
candidate_findings.impact: The plan provides no deterministic test that distinguishes a compliant checkpoint state machine from one that pauses, escalates, or resumes incorrectly.

candidate_findings.title: Gap classification and high-risk confirmation rules are nondeterministic
candidate_findings.statement: HITL-037 enumerates gap classes and narrow user-blocking grounds, but it does not define evidence sufficiency, safe-inference criteria, precedence when multiple classes apply, or when listed and similarly high-risk decisions require confirmation rather than merely may require it.
candidate_findings.impact: Controllers can classify the same uncertainty differently, either over-blocking ordinary work or silently proceeding through decisions that should require explicit authority.

candidate_findings.title: Approval exception artifacts lack typed lifecycle contracts
candidate_findings.statement: testing_policy_override and user_approved_incomplete_item have required conceptual contents, but the window supplies no field types, wire or persistence format, identity and scope matching rules, approval evidence format, mutation or revocation rules, expiration evaluation, reopen transition, or validation failures.
candidate_findings.impact: Testing can be restricted or incomplete work accepted using incompatible, stale, forged, or non-enforceable records despite nominally including the listed information.

candidate_findings.title: Typed authority blocker behavior is unnamed
candidate_findings.statement: Privileged installs and material external effects may become a typed blocker, but no blocker type, required payload, state transition, permitted actions, authority check, or resolution evidence is specified in this unit.
candidate_findings.impact: Builder-defined blocker behavior can strand execution, allow unsafe silent installation, or fail to preserve an auditable authority decision.

candidate_findings.title: HITL-037 excludes explicit user decisions from GUI coverage
candidate_findings.statement: The unit prescribes asking users and obtaining explicit confirmation yet classifies itself gui_related false and provides no interaction-surface acceptance criteria.
candidate_findings.impact: User-decision prompts, risk disclosure, confirmation controls, and accessible presentation can be omitted from GUI planning and validation.

candidate_findings.title: PAUSE.md validity and evaluation semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The gate lists frontmatter field names and precedence, but valid is not defined through field types, required-versus-null rules, scope grammar, action-id matching, timestamp format and clock, expiry boundary, file discovery and refresh behavior, malformed-file handling, or atomic removal semantics.
candidate_findings.impact: A safety gate can fail open or fail closed across implementations, allowing forbidden mutations or indefinitely blocking permitted work.

candidate_findings.title: HITLRequest remains an explicitly deferred partial schema
candidate_findings.statement: The request contract lists fields, one enum, and correlation prose, but does not provide field types, wire format, identifier rules, request-kind-specific requirements, allowed/default action invariants, version semantics, or validation and failure behavior; the same core explicitly says this critical row still requires a dedicated schema/detail lane and claims no closure.
candidate_findings.impact: Producers, providers, persistence, GUI consumers, and runtime handlers cannot exchange or validate one interoperable request object, making approval authority and expiry behavior unsafe and unauditable.

candidate_findings.title: Provider correlation fields have an unresolved object-shape ambiguity
candidate_findings.statement: The HITLRequest field list includes only provider_correlation_id, while provider-native correlation additionally stores provider_id, provider_request_id, and provider_thread_id; the window does not say whether these are top-level, nested, referenced elsewhere, or subject to the request schema. Optional markers also coexist with a rule that absence is represented by null fields.
candidate_findings.impact: Serializers can produce incompatible shapes or omit correlation needed to resume the provider-native request, and validators cannot distinguish a valid null representation from a missing field.

candidate_findings.title: pause_override has no authorized transition against PAUSE precedence
candidate_findings.statement: pause_override is a request kind, while PAUSE can be bypassed only when its allowed_action_ids already contains the exact action; no contract explains who may request or approve pause_override, what it changes, or whether it can ever authorize an action absent from the gate.
candidate_findings.impact: The label can become an unsafe ad hoc bypass or a permanently ineffective request kind, undermining the stated operator-gate authority.

candidate_findings.title: Skip and abort commands define payload names but not command behavior
candidate_findings.statement: The commands list fields and reuse unspecified existing semantics, but this window provides no field types, reason_code enumeration, authorization, valid source states, idempotency key or duplicate behavior, race handling, response or emitted event, persistence evidence, or failure contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Retries or concurrent execution can skip the wrong node, abort inconsistently, or report success without durable state and audit evidence.

candidate_findings.title: Timeout mapping and retry semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: Exact default durations and a terminal state are named, but the request-kind-to-action mapping is not enumerated and the window does not define the timeout start instant, expires_at_utc precedence, clock behavior, cancellation race, retry_request identity or timer reset, or how cancel_or_skip selects a command.
candidate_findings.impact: The same request can expose different post-expiry authorities or expire at different times, and retries can duplicate or resurrect stale approvals.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The window explicitly prevents HITL-035 from inventing local action names or independent ask-flow and terminal state machines and assigns shared-state-machine consumption without re-ownership.
The retired HITL-001 bridge has an explicit non-product disposition, a replacement owner range, a retired compile mode, and a create_worknodes false instruction.
HITL-036 explicitly keeps default correctness hands-off, makes checkpoints opt-in, and forbids replacement or short-circuiting of internal repair and assurance loops absent configured policy.
HITL-037 explicitly rejects ordinary uncertainty, casual opt-out inference, broad TODO permission, and blocking on details resolvable through evidence, safe defaults, or downstream stages.
PAUSE-versus-HITL precedence and the exact-action exception are explicit.
The six request_kind values are explicitly enumerated, and provider correlation explicitly forbids invented local identifiers.
The skip and abort command namespaces and their prohibition on unqualified UI payload names are exact.
Both timeout defaults, their millisecond values, the hitl_request_expired result label, and the three possible follow-up action labels are explicit.
The FABLE addendum does not claim runtime implementation, PNC-019 evidence, or a passing buildability gate.

unknowns.statement: The exact shared permission ladder, question model, blocked-episode transitions, and tool-permission behavior cannot be determined from this window because they are only referenced as external owned contracts.
The exact PS-116 critical-escalation policy, Goal Runtime autonomy policy, and OP-024 consumer obligation are outside this window and were not inspected.
It is unknown whether a checkpoint configuration schema or state machine exists elsewhere; none is supplied by this assigned core.
It is unknown whether provider_id, provider_request_id, and provider_thread_id belong inside HITLRequest, inside a nested correlation object, or in a separate provider record.
The existing skip and abort semantics consumed by the namespaced commands are outside this window, so their preconditions, transitions, and outcomes were not verified.
The behavior actually checked by the named plan and ledger validators is unknown because only their command names, not validator definitions or receipts, are inside the allowed scope.
The request-kind-specific assignment of view_details, retry_request, and cancel_or_skip cannot be determined from the phrase according to request kind.

canonical_text: 'The controller answers auto-resolvable gaps from evidence, applies safe defaults with recorded assumptions, and defers downstream-only details; it asks the user only for genuine product direction, risk acceptance, destructive authority, credentials, legal policy, or irreconcilable ambiguity. Security, data destruction, billing, migration, legal/compliance, irreversible external effects, or similarly high-risk decisions may require explicit user confirmation under HITL policy.

Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, and reopen conditions.

Global or privileged installation, paid services, license acceptance, account creation, credential use, device enrollment, or material external effects require applicable authority and may become a typed blocker rather than an unsafe silent
  install.

The only permitted incomplete item is a user_approved_incomplete_item naming the exact artifact and span, reason, risk, approver, downstream disposition, expiration or reopen condition, and evidence; broad permission to leave TODOs is invalid.

Classify gaps as auto_resolvable, safe_default_with_assumption, defer_to_plan_compile, defer_to_worknode_system, requires_user_policy_decision, requires_user_risk_acceptance, requires_external_credential, or true infrastructure/runtime blocker. Only product policy with no safe inference, material risk acceptance, destructive or irreversible operations, credentials or permissions, legal/compliance authority, or irreconcilable user preference conflicts may block for user decision.'

This addendum is canonical HITL spec text for deferred non-runtime FABLE rows. It creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, runtime artifacts, implementation files, production build tasks, final manifests, or PNC-019 receipts, and it does not mark `buildability_gate_passed` true.

`PAUSE.md` is a project-root operator gate file with frontmatter fields `pause_id`, `scope`, `reason`, `created_by`, `created_at_utc`, `expires_at_utc?`, and `allowed_action_ids[]`. A valid PAUSE gate blocks new mutating execution in scope until removed or expired. HITL approvals cannot override an active PAUSE gate unless `allowed_action_ids[]` includes the exact requested action. If both PAUSE and HITL are active, PAUSE precedence is evaluated first, then HITL approval.

`HITLRequest` fields are `hitl_request_id`, `request_kind`, `provider_correlation_id?`, `run_id?`, `attempt_id?`, `target_ref`, `permission_snapshot_id?`, `allowed_action_ids[]`, `default_action_id?`, `expires_at_utc?`, `request_copy_ref`, `created_at_utc`, and `schema_version`.
`request_kind` values are `approval`, `clarification`, `risk_acceptance`, `pause_override`, `credential_required`, and `manual_review`.

Provider-native correlation stores `provider_correlation_id`, `provider_id`, `provider_request_id?`, and `provider_thread_id?` only when supplied by the provider; absence is represented by null fields, not invented local ids.

- Skip node command: `cmd.runtime.skip_node` with fields `node_id`, `run_id`, `reason_code`, and `operator_note?`.
- Cancel run command: `cmd.runtime.abort_run` with fields `run_id`, `reason_code`, `requested_by`, and `created_at_utc`.
- These commands consume existing skip/abort semantics and must not be renamed to unqualified `skip_node` or `abort_run` in UI command payloads.

- `approval_wait` default timeout is `3600000` ms (1 hour).
- `long_governance_wait` default timeout is `86400000` ms (24 hours).
- Timeout maps to `hitl_request_expired` and allowed actions `view_details`, `retry_request`, and `cancel_or_skip` according to request kind.
